October 5, 2026

US military buildup in Israel points to renewed strikes on Iran

tags: war, politics, defence
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Flight tracking data shows C-17 military transport aircraft moving US equipment and personnel into Israel. An Israeli outlet, WALA, reported a large concentration of American military resources in the region, with roughly 3,000 US troops stationed there and a further 10,000 said to be on the way. The movements are being read as preparation for a renewed round of US strikes on Iran.

Hegseth announces sweeping changes to US military posture

tags: defence, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth delivered a speech to the Department of Defense announcing sweeping changes to the United States military, including the possibility of redeploying forces from Europe to the Western Hemisphere. The staging and imagery of the address drew widespread online comparison to the presentation style of authoritarian governments past and present.

Trump calls US elections corrupt as advisers warn of bleak polling

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

Donald Trump posted through the night attacking the way American elections are counted, calling the process corrupt and comparing it unfavourably with Brazil, in a post that initially referred to India before being deleted. The outburst comes as advisers privately tell him polling ahead of the midterms is increasingly poor. He has floated $5,000 dividend payments, $500 rebate cheques aimed primarily at swing states via Obamacare funds, and $100 cheques to 20 million seniors toward Medicare costs, while warning states that voting against him would make him less inclined to help them.

House Democrats file articles of impeachment against Trump

tags: politics, legal
sources: @carolinegleich

House Democrats have filed formal articles of impeachment against President Trump. The charges include using the presidency for personal profit, misusing the pardon power, going to war with Iran without congressional approval, deploying troops into American cities, and defying court orders. The current Congress has repeatedly voted to set the articles aside. A June poll found 53% of Americans believe there are grounds for impeachment, with corruption the most commonly cited reason.

Brazil presidential race heads to runoff after Flávio Bolsonaro wins first round

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews

Flávio Bolsonaro took 47.24% of the first-round vote in Brazil's presidential election with 98.81% of ballots counted, ahead of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on 44.91%. Neither candidate cleared 50%, sending the race to an October 25 runoff. Bolsonaro, the son of jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro, has pledged to pardon his father and others convicted over the January 8, 2023 riots, and has proposed spending cuts, tougher anti-gang policies and closer ties with the United States. Lula, seeking a fourth term, described the election as a choice between democracy and barbarism.

KKK leadership claims surging support ahead of US midterms

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

Ku Klux Klan leadership says support for the organisation is growing rapidly ahead of the United States midterm elections, according to a new Al Jazeera investigation. Leaders attribute the increase to the spread of white nationalism on social media and the current political climate, and describe an attempted rebrand centred on family and faith that is drawing young white men. The claim is difficult to quantify independently and rests on the assertions of the group's own leadership.

Leaked audio captures Ken Paxton saying he has little control over his Senate campaign

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

Politico has obtained unearthed audio of Texas attorney general Ken Paxton saying he has never been in a race where he felt less control over the campaign. In the recording Paxton says messaging and the issues that matter are coming from Washington, that he does not control them and has no ability to change anything. Texas voters have polled in favour of a candidate independent of Washington, making the admission a potential factor in the state's Senate race.

Sam Altman says the world should accept that bad things will happen with AI

tags: tech, ai
sources: @aaronparnas

OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said in an interview that people should accept that bad things will happen with artificial intelligence, naming hacks, scams and other harms, in exchange for the technology's benefits. He pointed to gains such as medical breakthroughs in healthcare. The remarks follow warnings from a researcher who resigned from rival firm Anthropic that AI could pose an existential risk by the end of the decade.

Montreal approves bylaw banning insults aimed at police and city employees

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

Montreal city council voted 35-25 to approve a bylaw prohibiting insults, harassment, threats and other abusive conduct toward police officers and municipal employees, with no start date announced. First offences carry fines of $300 to $1,000, rising to $2,000 for repeat violations, and city workers could refuse service, though the bylaw does not define what counts as an insult. Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada said the city needed to act after reports of increased abuse of employees, while civil rights groups and opposition councillors warn the measure could restrict free expression and hand police broad enforcement discretion.

Russia quarantines hundreds after suspected plague exposure at Siberian lab

tags: health
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Russian health authorities have placed hundreds of people in quarantine over a suspected plague outbreak after a 28-year-old laboratory technician died at a Siberian institute. A test tube containing a plague pathogen is reported to have broken over the researcher's hands. Russian state media has denied the death was caused by the pathogen even as the quarantine proceeds, and other health experts say the cause has not been determined. US authorities say they are monitoring the situation and will advise citizens if it becomes a genuine concern.

US Coast Guard returns fire after shots from Mexican side of Rio Grande

tags: immigration, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

US Coast Guard personnel returned fire during a federal operation near Garceno, Texas, after shots were fired from the Mexican side of the Rio Grande. No US personnel were injured. Officials have not identified who fired the initial shots.

US Marine arrested in Okinawa over hotel death as Japan protests

tags: legal, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

A US Marine stationed in Okinawa has been arrested on suspicion of robbery and murder after a 39-year-old woman was found dead in a hotel in Naha. Police say Anna Yagi died from asphyxiation. Lance Cpl. Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, denies the allegations. Japan has lodged a formal protest with the United States.

New York operation locates 34 missing children across Queens and Long Island

tags: policing, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Governor Kathy Hochul announced that 34 missing children were located during a 72-hour operation across Queens and Long Island, ending disappearances that had lasted from a few days to as long as ten years. The children were aged between 7 and 18; officials said many were runaways and some had been exposed to human trafficking and exploitation. The breakdown given to Newsday included 18 from Nassau County, 12 from Suffolk County and four from Queens, with 31 further local cases still open. More than 100 professionals from nearly 40 state agencies took part.

Fox News hires former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt

tags: media, politics
sources: @groundnews

Fox News has hired Karoline Leavitt, who served as White House press secretary, as an on-air contributor beginning November 1, The New York Times reported. She joins a roster that already includes Dana Perino and Kayleigh McEnany, both of whom held the same post. Fox News Media chief executive Suzanne Scott cited Leavitt's firsthand White House and campaign experience, while Leavitt said she would bring the candour that defined her tenure with the Trump administration. The hire follows repeated public complaints from President Trump about the network's coverage.
